_about: Cases for tests/parser_eval.py. Each is self-contained: it carries the
settings it starts from, so a wrong answer at case 3 cannot corrupt case
30 and the set can run in any order, or in parallel.
A case is one of:
expect: {field: value}   a delta. The value may be a single value, a
list meaning any of these, or {min, max} for
the relative asks that have no one right
answer - 'a bit more contrast' is correct
anywhere in a band, and pinning it to one
number would score the prompt on a coin flip.
expect: "decline"        refusing is the right answer.
now / before  the config the utterance is resolved against, and the one
it had before that. Only 'undo' needs 'before', and only
because undo is meaningless without it.
allow         fields that may also appear without being counted wrong.
A named look is a judgement, not a lookup: 'the Matrix'
must be green, and a ramp choice alongside is reasonable.
forbid        fields that must not appear.
or_decline    declining is also acceptable. Used where the request is
impossible to satisfy exactly - either a sensible clamp
or an honest refusal is a good answer, and insisting on
one would be scoring taste.

cases.note: The floor. If this fails nothing else matters.

cases.utterance: green, high contrast, and the fine character set
back to plain greyscale and unfreeze
unfreeze it, and while you're there make it cyan
cases.note: Two asks in one sentence, the second parenthetical.
Warm on this device means amber or lime, per the prompt.

cases.utterance: that's too punchy, flatten it out
bigger characters on the little screen
cases.note: Panel glyph size, not the character ramp. Confusing the two is the likeliest wrong answer here.
A bit. Doubling it would be wrong; so would 1.01.
Paired with the case above: the two must differ, or the model is ignoring the modifier.
One of the doc's four awkward ones. Meaningless without `before`.
Undo when the last change touched two fields.

cases.note2: allow covers every other field: 'everything' means everything, and resetting one of them is not a mistake.

cases.utterance: make it look like the Matrix
cases.note: The doc's example. Green is the point; anything else alongside is taste.

cases.utterance: make it look like an old cash machine
make it look like a Kindle
cases.note: E-ink on paper. The light-screen schemes are the point.
Deliberately vague. A wide set of right answers, but not every answer.

cases.utterance: put it on the little screen only
same but on the big screen
cases.note: The doc's example. 'Same but' means change only the display.
Monitor, not panel. A synonym the prompt names.

cases.utterance: make it green and turn the volume up
cases.note: Do the half that maps, say what does not. Declining the whole thing is wrong.

cases.utterance: warmer, and email the picture to my sister
zoom in a bit and make it amber
cases.note: There is no zoom. fill crops, which is close but not the same - so it is allowed, not required. (The allow entry was missing on the first run and the case failed on its own omission, not the model's answer.)
The doc's example. A parser that always answers cannot be scored on this.

cases.utterance: how many colour schemes are there
cases.note: A question, not an instruction. Answering it by changing the scheme would be wrong.
Impossible exactly. Either an honest refusal or a sensible nearest is fine; an invalid delta is not.

cases.utterance: turn the contrast up to eleven
cases.note: Spinal Tap. Clamping to the maximum is the good answer.
No sepia. Refuse, or offer the nearest warm one - but never emit 'sepia'.

cases.utterance: give me a thousand colour levels
cases.note: Clamp to the ceiling, or say no. Emitting 1000 would be the schema failing to guide it.

cases.utterance: set the contrast to minus five
cases.note: Nonsense value. The floor is 0.1.
